source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Seedling blight (ជម្ងឺស្លាកស្លឹកលើកូនពោត, Seedling Blights): this disease occurs on young corn seedlings, causing damage to the stem and roots. Symptoms of this disease can cause the seedling to wilt and collapse. If corn seed that already carries this pathogen is planted, or if the seed coat is weak/thin, the seedling that germinates from it is more likely to be damaged by this disease.

Seeds with weak seed coats, seeds that carry latent fungal infection, can cause seedling blight in the same way as described above. This blight is closely linked to the health of the seedling. It commonly occurs when corn is planted in conditions that are not timed well with rainfall. In dry/cracked soil, or soil that has crusted hard, this can further encourage seedling blight. Blight of this type spreads readily to seedlings, causing leaf wilting, curling, and drying, and can affect the root system's ability to establish during the germination stage. This disease is commonly seen in April and early May.

Prevention and control measures include:
- Take proper care of seed lots.
- Ensure adequate soil drainage.
- Remove and destroy infected seedlings showing disease symptoms.
